rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for fiddling with something to try to fix or improve it.

example.english: I often tinker with my phone's settings to see if I can save battery.
example.traditional: 我成日搞部手機啲設定，睇下可唔可以慳啲電。
example.jyutping: ngo5 seng4 jat6 gaau2 bou6 sau2 gei1 di1 cit3 ding6 tai2 haa5 ho2 m4 ho2 ji5 haan1 di1 din6

rows.note: Use this when the tinkering specifically involves physically repairing or adjusting an object, machine, or device.

example.english: The fan is broken, so I'll try to tinker with it myself.
example.traditional: 部風扇壞咗，我試下自己整。
example.jyutping: bou6 fung1 sin3 waai6 zo2 ngo5 si3 haa5 zi6 gei2 zing2

rows.note: This is the all-purpose casual way to express having a go at fixing or making something.

example.english: The fan is broken; I'll tinker with it first.
example.traditional: 部風扇壞咗，我試下整先。
example.jyutping: bou6 fung1 sin3 waai6 zo2 ngo5 si3 haa6 zing2 sin1

rows.note: Use this noun phrase for a person who repairs or makes things, rather than for the repair attempt itself.

example.english: He's a tinker who can fix anything broken at home.
example.traditional: 佢係個整電器嘅人，屋企啲壞嘢都畀佢搞掂。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai6 go3 zing2 din6 hei3 ge3 jan4 uk1 kei2 di1 waai6 je5 dou1 bei2 keoi5 gaau2 dim6
